A Classic Brownstone Love Story.
Some homes simply exist. Others hold stories. For over 70 years, 29 Clifton Place has been both - a multigenerational residence cherished by the same family for three generations, quietly standing on one of Clinton Hill's most beloved blocks. Now, this classic brownstone presents a rare opportunity to begin its next chapter.

Spanning approximately 2,700 square feet across three floors, with a full basement bringing the total to nearly 3,600 square feet, the home offers the scale and proportions that define classic brownstone Brooklyn. Currently configured as a garden duplex with an upper residence, the layout has long allowed the flexibility of two kitchens while functioning comfortably as a single extended home. Today, it presents a myriad of possibilities - from maintaining the current configuration with income potential, to creating a spectacular single-unit residence designed entirely around your vision.

Built 20 feet wide on a 100-foot lot, the home enjoys 1,330 square feet of exterior space between the private backyard and charming front courtyard. Inside, a remarkable collection of preserved architectural details reveals the craftsmanship of another era. Five original marble fireplaces, elegant plaster ceiling medallions, chair rail moldings, and arched transitions between rooms speak to the home's historic character. Oversized windows bathe the interiors in natural light, while original pocket doors, shutters, and the sweeping wood staircase with its original banister and spindles connect the three levels with quiet grandeur.

Whether one chooses to undertake a thoughtful restoration that honors the home's historic soul while introducing modern comforts, or a complete reimagination into a contemporary showpiece, the foundation is undeniable: a house with extraordinary bones and timeless proportions ready to be shaped into something exceptional. Adding to the possibilities, the property retains approximately 1,380 square feet of unused FAR, creating the opportunity to expand and add even more living space. The result could be a dramatic four-story single-unit home approaching 4,900 square feet, or an expansive owner's triplex residence with a garden rental - a flexibility that allows the home to evolve with your lifestyle.

Beyond the home itself lies the undeniable charm of Clifton Place, a quiet one-way, tree-lined street that has long been considered one of Clinton Hill's hidden gems Part of the Clinton Hill Historic District, the block is defined by cohesive rows of 19th-century brownstones that together create a streetscape rich in character and architectural heritage. Despite its peaceful setting, everything you need is moments away. Neighborhood favorites like Entre Nous Wine Bar, Choice Market, Peaches, and Clementine Bakery are just around the corner, while Food Emporium, Starbucks, and a 24-hour attended garage add everyday convenience. Transportation is equally effortless with nearby subway lines and buses connecting you easily to the rest of Brooklyn and Manhattan.

Classic brownstone Brooklyn. A coveted block.

Endless potential. For those searching for a home that can grow with them - a place where history, character, and possibility meet - 29 Clifton Place may be the perfect place to begin your next chapter. Find your sweet spot.

A Rare Pre-War Gem in Greenpoint - Introducing 51 Apollo Street

Built in 1899, this classic brick townhouse sits on a quiet, tree-lined block moments from everything Greenpoint has to offer. Set on a 19' x 100' lot, this is a home that has truly stood the test of time.

Currently configured as a lovingly preserved single-family residence, the property spans approximately 2,850 square feet across two primary floors and a substantial basement. Original details include soaring 10-foot ceilings on the first floor, hardwood floors, intricate moldings, and beautiful stained glass accents that reflect the craftsmanship of the era. The home also benefits from natural light through both its East and West exposures.

The first floor opens with a stately foyer and hallway that immediately showcase the home's scale and original architectural details. Beyond, a grand living room stretches nearly 24 feet in length, setting the tone for the rest of the home. The library, along with the second-floor home office, features stunning stained glass panels that softly filter light between rooms. The rear kitchen offers a charming pass-through window overlooking the dining room and a classic swinging door, a nod to the home's pre-war heritage that is as functional as it is full of character. Through the rear door, step out onto the terrace and garden beyond, providing generous outdoor space on this deep 100-foot lot. A full bathroom with shower sits conveniently off the main hall.

Upstairs, 9'6" ceilings continue the sense of grandeur. The primary bedroom spans an impressive 23'10" and is accompanied by two additional bedrooms, a dedicated office, a second kitchen, and a full bathroom with tub. Two stained-glass skylights introduce beautiful filtered light and serve as one of the home’s most distinctive original features.

The basement offers one of the home’s most compelling opportunities: a nearly full-footprint space measuring 47'5" x 18'1" with 7'6" ceilings. This expansive level includes three custom built cedar closets, washer/dryer hookups, a private garden-level entrance, and a second egress through steel doors directly to the backyard. Whether envisioned as a recreation room, home gym, creative studio, or expanded living space, the basement provides a flexible foundation for a wide range of uses.

With approximately 2,850 square feet of interior space, 950 square feet of private outdoor space, 10-foot parlor ceilings, and original pre-war details intact, 51 Apollo Street presents a rare opportunity to own a piece of Greenpoint history. Buyers may explore maintaining the home as a grand single-family residence, converting it into two units as seen in neighboring properties, or potentially expanding with the property's remaining FAR. All prospective buyers must verify any development potential, conversions, or expansion plans with their architect and the appropriate authorities.

Built in 1908 by architect James Gordon Riley, 36 Gramercy Park East is a celebrated Gothic Revival architectural landmark. The twelve-story building is clad in white terra-cotta adorned with ornate Gothic arches, colonnettes, shields, cherubs, and gargoyles. A dramatic central courtyard creates the appearance of twin towers, while two cast-stone armored knights holding spears stand guard at the entrance. 

This award-winning full-service building is illuminated by custom gas lanterns—faithful replicas of those that originally graced the property in 1908. The lobby is rich with old-world detail, featuring onyx and terra-cotta finishes, a decorative frieze, and an extraordinary ornamental filigree ceiling.

Over the years, notable residents have included actor John Barrymore, sculptor Daniel Chester French, Alfred Ringling of circus fame, and playwright Eugene O’Neill. 

The building offers a 24-hour doorman and concierge, common laundry room, and welcomes pets. Additional private storage available for sale. Residents also enjoy close proximity to the Union Square Greenmarket, exceptional dining and shopping, and convenient access to public transportation.

Perfectly situated in Rosario Candela's most coveted building, 740 Park Avenue, this palatial sixteen-into-fourteen-room southwest corner duplex is a true architectural masterpiece. Drenched in sunlight, the residence is distinguished by ceilings soaring to nearly 11 feet, three wood-burning fireplaces, and an extraordinary abundance of beautifully preserved historic detail. The home offers five bedrooms, five full bathrooms, and two powder rooms, along with grand entertaining rooms including a living room, formal dining room, conservatory, library, windowed eat-in kitchen and breakfast room, as well as an oversized staff room and windowed laundry room.

The residence unfolds across two levels and is defined by remarkable scale, elegant flow, and gracious entertaining spaces. Accessed via a private elevator landing, guests are welcomed into an impressive rectangular gallery, anchored by Candela's signature curved staircase ascending to the upper floor. From the gallery, a magnificent suite of entertaining rooms unfolds in perfect sequence. The expansive corner living room and richly paneled library, each with a wood-burning fireplace, face south and are bathed in natural light throughout the day while enjoying wonderfully open city views. The living room also captures western outlooks over St. James' Church toward Central Park . There is an impressive formal dining room, ideal for large-scale gatherings, with an adjoining conservatory that connects gracefully to the living room. An elegant powder room and coat closet are off the gallery.

The expansive windowed eat-in kitchen is thoughtfully designed with ample room for dining and is complemented by a separate windowed breakfast room. The kitchen has a well-appointed service pantry, staff bedroom and bath, laundry room, and an additional powder room. A discreet back staircase provides direct access to the upper level.

The upper floor is dedicated to the private quarters. The primary suite, formed by combining two bedrooms, occupies a prime southwest corner and houses the third wood-burning fireplace. It has an expansive windowed dressing room and an ensuite bath with two sinks, two water closets, a separate shower, and a soaking tub. Adjacent is a large south-facing bedroom with its own windowed bath and wet bar. Three additional generously scaled bedrooms, each with excellent closet space, are served by two additional windowed bathrooms.

The building allows no financing, and there is a 3% flip tax paid by the purchaser. A storage room and wine cellar are assigned to each apartment.

One of the most distinctive architectural features is the reinforced roof, allowing for seven commercial-grade skylights, filling the space with natural light and allowing for open, column-free entertaining. Significant additional capital improvements include new insulation, fresh stucco, custom copper detailing, curated exterior lighting, upgraded pavers, and refined balustrades, all contributing to the home's rare level of finish, functionality, and enduring value.

A private elevator opens directly into a skylit foyer, where French doors lead effortlessly onto the terrace. The natural flow of the living spaces supports both comfortable everyday living and large-scale hosting. The sun-flooded living room, centered around a wood-burning fireplace, is both warm and expansive, with seamless access outdoors and a discreet wet bar with Sub-Zero wine storage. The formal dining room sits just beyond, connecting to a chef's kitchen with custom cabinetry, stone and marble surfaces, an oversized skylit island, and top-tier appliances including an 8-burner range and Sub-Zero refrigerator. An adjoining media room and separate service entrance add convenience and flexibility.

The private bedroom wing offers two tranquil bedroom suites, each with direct terrace access. The primary suite features a walk-in closet and a skylit onyx bathroom with a soaking tub, rain shower, and radiant heated floors.
An elegant powder room, central air conditioning, vented washer/dryer, and integrated sound system complete this exceptional residence.

The sleek, contemporary kitchen features premium finishes and generous storage, making everyday cooking and entertaining a delight. On the main level there are two bedrooms and one full bathroom. Occupying a prominent corner within the landmarked O'Neill Building, Penthouse B is a premier duplex residence that balances Gilded Age scale with contemporary architectural precision. Originally constructed in 1887 as a premier department store in the Ladies' Mile historic district, the building was reimagined into a collection of luxury residences that retain the soaring volumes of its cast-iron heritage. This trophy home spans 4,819 square feet of interior space, complemented by a triple-terrace outdoor program totaling over 2,500 square feet.

The Great Room serves as the residence's focal point, spanning 53 feet in length and framed by over 220 linear feet of windows. High ceilings and a dual southern and eastern exposure provide superlative natural light and panoramic views of the Manhattan skyline. The layout is currently configured as a three-bedroom home but was originally designed for four true bedrooms, allowing for significant flexibility in how the space is utilized.

A signature element of the property is the historic gold-coated Neo-Grec cupola. One of only a handful remaining in New York, this 43-foot high belfry can be converted into a private media room or home office, offering a 360-degree architectural experience. The kitchen is designed for high-capacity entertaining, featuring a large center island, Viking and Sub-Zero appliances, a butler's pantry, and a separate breakfast room.

The upper level is dedicated to the primary suite, providing a secluded sanctuary with an oversized spa bath and two walk-in dressing rooms. This level opens onto a private terrace, one of three expansive outdoor spaces that wrap the home. Additional features include a private service entry, a dedicated 250-square-foot storage unit adjacent to the apartment, and a laundry room.

The O'Neill Building is a full-service condominium offering a 24-hour doorman, concierge, and a 4,000-square-foot common roof deck with an outdoor kitchen. Located in the heart of Chelsea, the building provides immediate access to the West Village and Flatiron, as well as many of the city's most established culinary and cultural destinations.
